Special attention or prominence given to something.

emphasis.ety: From Latin emphasis, from Ancient Greek ἔμφασις (émphasis, “significance”), from ἐμφαίνω (emphaínō, “to present; to indicate”), from ἐν- (en-, “in”) + φαίνω (phaínō, “to show”).

ex.ja: 彼はその問題を強調しすぎた。

ex.en: He placed emphasis on the importance of education.
ex.ja: 彼は教育の重要性を強調した。

ex.en: He put special emphasis on the problem.
ex.ja: 彼はその問題を特に強調した。

en: Morality.
The standards that govern the conduct of a person, especially a member of a profession.

ethics.ety: From Middle English etik, from Middle French ethique, from Late Latin ethica, from Ancient Greek ἠθική (ēthikḗ), from ἠθικός (ēthikós, “of or for morals, moral, expressing character”), from ἦθος (êthos, “character, moral nature”).

ex.en: Ethics means the rules of conduct.
ex.ja: 倫理学というのは、行動の規範を意味する。

ex.en: The paper discusses the problem in terms of ethics.
ex.ja: この論文は倫理学の面からその問題を論じている。

ex.en: A great many people were opposed to gene therapy in terms of ethics.
ex.ja: たくさんの人々が倫理の面から遺伝子治療に反対した。

en: The state of being excited (emotionally aroused).
Something that excites.

excitement.ety: From Middle English excitement, from Old French excitement, equivalent to excite + -ment.

ex.en: She turned over the page with excitement.
ex.ja: 彼女は興奮しながらページをめくった。

ex.en: The news of his arrival added to our excitement.
ex.ja: 彼の到着の知らせで我々の興奮は高まった。

ex.en: There was an air of excitement at the meeting.
ex.ja: 会議は熱気に包まれていた。

en: The process of exploring.
The process of penetrating, or ranging over for purposes of (especially geographical) discovery.

exploration.ety: From Middle French exploration, from Latin exploratio. Morphologically explore + -ation.

ex.en: He likes to go on explorations to Africa.
ex.ja: 彼はアフリカへ探検旅行に行くのが好きだ。

ex.en: Japan will soon start to engage in the exploration of the universe.
ex.ja: 日本はすぐに宇宙開発に乗り出すだろう。

ex.en: Voyages of exploration were the earliest in the history of studying the ocean.
ex.ja: 海洋研究の歴史の先駆けとなったのは、探検のための航海だった。

ex.ja: 彼のユーモアのセンスは非常によい。

ex.en: He seems to have no sense of humor.

en: A sight or view of the interior of anything; a deep inspection or view; introspection; frequently used with into.

insight.ety: From Middle English insight, insiht (“insight, mental vision, intelligence, understanding”), equivalent to in- + sight. Compare West Frisian ynsjoch (“insight”), Dutch inzicht (“insight, awareness, view, opinion”), German Low German Insicht (“insight”), German Einsicht (“insight, knowledge, perception, understanding”), Danish indsigt (“insight”), Swedish insikt (“insight”), Icelandic innsýn (“insight”).

ex.ja: 彼女は自分の洞察力という利益を彼らに与えてやった。

ex.ja: 彼は自分の洞察力という利益を彼らに与えてやった。

To give courage.
To give strength; to supply energy or vigour.

nerve.ety:

ex.en: His nerve failed him at the last moment.
ex.ja: いよいよという時になって彼は怖じ気付いた。

ex.ja: このワタクシをさらりと無視するとは良い度胸ですわね。

Reservation, nature preserve.
To protect; to keep from harm or injury.
To save from decay by the use of some preservative substance, such as sugar or salt; to season and prepare (fruits, meat, etc.) for storage.

preserve.ety: From Middle English preserven, from Old French preserver, from Medieval Latin prēservāre (“keep, preserve”), from Late Latin praeservāre (“guard beforehand”), from prae (“before”, adverb) + servāre (“maintain, keep”). Displaced native Old English nerian.

ex.ja: 善ならざるものは何であれ存続しえない。

ex.ja: この肉は保存がきく。

en: A quick hostile or predatory incursion or invasion in a battle.
An attack or invasion for the purpose of making arrests, seizing property, or plundering.
To engage in a raid against.
To lure from another; to entice away from.

raid.ety: From Scots raid, from Northern Middle English rade, from Old English rād (“a riding, an expedition on horseback, road”), whence also the inherited English road (“way, street”). The earlier senses of “a riding, expedition, raid” fell into disuse in Early Modern English, but were revived in the northern form raid by Walter Scott in the early 19th century. The use for a swift police operation appears in the later 19th century and may perhaps have been influenced by French razzia (similar in both original meaning and sound).

ex.en: The main office was raided by the police.
ex.ja: 本店は警察の手入れを受けた。

ex.en: The house was raided by the police.
ex.ja: その家は警察の手入れをうけた。

To collide with (an object), usually with the intention of damaging it or disabling its function.
To strike (something) hard, especially with an implement.
Rancid; offensive in smell or taste.

ram.ety: From Middle English ram, rom, ramme, from Old English ramm (“ram”), from Proto-Germanic *rammaz (“ram”), possibly from *rammaz (“strong”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Rom (“ram”), Dutch ram (“a male sheep”), German Ramm, Ramme (“ram”). Possibly akin also to Danish ram (“sharp; acrid; rank”), Swedish ram (“strong; perfect”), Faroese ramur (“strong; competent”), Icelandic rammur (“strong; sturdy”).

ex.ja: 彼らはそれぞれの家に帰った。

To consider (a function) as defined on a subset of its original domain.

acknowledge.ety:

The /k/-sound was preserved by being redistributed to the preceding syllable: /əˈkn-/ > /əkˈn-/. The -c- was inserted accordingly to reflect this pronunciation more clearly.
